architecture.non_duplication_rule: The Guide references machine contracts from the POLIS Specification and does not define competing package layouts or apply semantics.

sdd: Define observable behavior, invariants, trust boundaries, scope, non-goals, and failure semantics before implementation.
Revise the versioned specification before changing a machine contract.
Treat accepted specifications as normative until explicitly superseded.
tdd: Observe a behavior-specific Red result before the production change when the behavior is testable that way.
Run the new test, affected tests, and complete policy gates.
Refactor only while protected behavior remains green.

portable_trust_boundary.bounded_input: Treat .polis bytes as untrusted and reject archives, members, evidence lines, and command output exceeding normative bounds.
portable_trust_boundary.scope: Change Contract v2+ declares scope.allowed_paths; strict v3/v4 additionally declare test_scope, and producer plus consumer validate authorized paths.
portable_trust_boundary.environment: Every executable schema-v3 command declares inherit or clean environment semantics; clean passes only named variables and never serializes values.
portable_trust_boundary.evidence: V6 command evidence persists byte counts, SHA-256 digests, truncation state, command identity, environment names, and semantic oracle results instead of raw stdout/stderr; each policy execution also records its effective validation level and complete enabled/disabled project-gate inventory.
portable_trust_boundary.authentication: Detached Ed25519 signatures authenticate SHA-256 of exact .polis bytes when the consumer supplies a trusted public key; package contents never define trust roots.
portable_trust_boundary.preflight: Consumer preflight repeats package, repository baseline, isolated validation, target-tree, scope, packaged policy, and git apply --check without applying the payload. Apply never reuses a previous preflight result.
portable_trust_boundary.development: V6 requires a strict schema-v3 Specification draft to be locked by polis start into schema v4 before implementation. The canonical zero-residue path supplies Project Policy schema v3 explicitly from outside the target repository and locks its canonical SHA-256. New builds accept only schema v4. Feature/defect use Red-to-Green; behavior-preserving uses Green-to-Green; REQ-to-AC proof traceability and captured-test immutability are mandatory.
portable_trust_boundary.target_residue: Canonical external-policy execution leaves no tool-owned files, configuration, linked-worktree administration, persistent temporary Git objects, or evidence metadata in the target repository. Temporary validation state and default apply evidence live outside the target and are removed before successful return.

delivery_workflow: Orient and resolve repository identity, permissions, objective, changed behavior, protected behavior, compatibility surface, and non-goals.
Inspect tests, architecture, contracts, CI, release tooling, current policy requirements, and relevant runtime evidence.

Resolve an effective Project Policy schema v3 and choose its validation reinforcement level before delivery work. Strict remains the default; standard and minimal may reduce only explicitly identified project-quality gates, with reasons. For the canonical zero-residue path, keep it outside the target repository; polis init --dry-run may generate validated policy JSON without creating .polis. A committed .polis/policy.json remains a compatibility option, not a requirement.
Write or revise the versioned behavior Specification and external strict Change Contract schema-v3 draft before production implementation.

Run polis start --policy <external-policy> on the clean committed baseline to produce the mandatory locked schema-v4 contract. The lock binds canonical effective-policy bytes by SHA-256; do not implement before this state transition.

For feature/defect work, add the test-only Red delta and run polis capture-red with the locked v4 contract before production implementation. For behavior-preserving work, keep the characterization command Green on the locked baseline.
Implement bounded Red-Green-Refactor slices while preserving captured strict test bytes, declared test_scope, and scope.

Run repository-required affected and complete validation using the same effective Project Policy. Record the selected level and actual enabled/disabled gate inventory; structural, integrity, security, baseline, scope, exact-tree, development-proof, and transactional-apply invariants remain mandatory.

Invoke polis build --policy <same-effective-policy> only with the locked schema-v4 contract and regression patch exactly when Red-to-Green requires it. Reject policy hash drift before accepting the artifact.
Accept an artifact only after canonical polis verify; use polis inspect for validated metadata and REQ-to-AC proof traceability.

Before mutation, run polis preflight against the exact consumer baseline. Then use polis apply, which repeats validation, consumes the packaged policy, preserves HEAD/index, and leaves no default tool-owned target-repository state.
Treat GitHub Release publication as a separate explicit operation after source validation and commit; run publisher preflight without --publish first.
non_goals: parallel or DAG gates without measured need
claiming hermetic builds from environment filtering
inventing language-specific init commands without repository evidence

v6_contracts.change_contract_schema: schema v4 locked is mandatory for new V6 builds; schemas v1-v3 are read-compatible migration inputs only
invariants: strict coverage greater than the declared threshold
fail closed on unproven mandatory conditions
effective policy hash bound independently of repository pathname
zero tool-specific target residue after successful canonical external-policy execution

change_contract_supported_schemas.rule: Reader compatibility MUST NOT authorize a new legacy producer build.
